findings.title: verify() never checks session expiry
findings.description: verify only matches the token and ignores expires_at, so expired sessions remain valid contrary to its documented behavior.

findings.title: require_admin always returns false
findings.description: Condition `session.role != "admin" || session.role != "owner"` is true for every possible role, so no session can ever pass.

findings.title: bearer_token assumes a space and fixed 64-byte buffer
findings.description: strchr may return nullptr when no space is present (then space+1 dereferences nullptr), and strcpy into char[64] overflows on long headers, causing crashes/UB.

findings.title: Cache::set leaks the previous entry for an existing code
findings.description: When code already exists, the old Entry* is overwritten without deletion, and limit_==0 causes erase(begin()) on an empty map (UB).

findings.title: Eviction does not select the least recently used entry
findings.description: Erasing entries_.begin() evicts by map key order, not by used timestamp, contradicting the documented LRU behavior.

findings.title: sweep() invalidates its iterator
findings.description: Erasing while incrementing the loop iterator is undefined behavior and can skip entries or crash.

findings.title: Cache destructor leaks Entry* objects
findings.description: entries_.clear() destroys pointers without deleting, leaking every cached entry.

findings.title: utilization() loses precision via integer division
findings.description: `size / limit * 100` evaluates to 0 unless the cache is completely full.

findings.title: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS is treated as seconds, not milliseconds
findings.description: The value is parsed as milliseconds per docs/comments but assigned directly to Seconds, making timeouts 1000x too long; ms==0 also assigns zero instead of keeping default.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is treated as seconds, not milliseconds
findings.description: Cache TTL from milliseconds is assigned directly to Seconds, inflating TTL 1000x.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but discarded
findings.description: `parsed` is cast to void and cfg.fetch_limit is never updated, so the env setting has no effect.

findings.title: validate() always returns true
findings.description: Even when problems are recorded it returns true, so invalid configs are not rejected at startup.

findings.title: format_row returns dangling pointer to stack buffer
findings.description: Returning `char row[128]` address yields UB; callers observe garbage or crashes.

findings.title: write_snapshot uses fixed /tmp path and cross-filesystem rename
findings.description: Concurrent calls collide on the same temp path and std::rename fails when /tmp is a different filesystem from dir, leaving snapshot unwritten.

findings.title: Metrics::errors_ is uninitialized
findings.description: errors_ has no default initializer unlike resolved_/created_, so errors() returns indeterminate value.

findings.title: stats() divides by store size without zero check
findings.description: When the store is empty, total_hits()/size() divides by zero, crashing the stats endpoint.

findings.title: resolve() deletes live links and accepts expired ones
findings.description: Condition `Clock::now() < expires_at` erases the link when it is still valid and lets expired links resolve, the opposite of intended behavior.

findings.title: rename() validates `from` twice and does not validate `to`
findings.description: validate_code(from) is called twice while the new code (to) is never validated, allowing invalid destination codes.

findings.title: page() off-by-one end index
findings.description: `end = all.size()+1` can read one past the vector end (and includes a phantom element).

findings.title: success_rate() truncates to 0 due to integer division
findings.description: `used / links_.size() * 100` is 0 unless every link has hits.

findings.title: remove() does not return the owner's quota slot
findings.description: Documented to decrement quota, but it never touches quota_, so deleted links still count against the owner.

findings.title: top() returns least-followed links in possibly oversized vector
findings.description: Sorts ascending so resize(n) yields the lowest-hit links, and n beyond size value-initializes phantom entries.

findings.title: by_owner() matches substrings instead of exact owner
findings.description: `owner.find(owner)` returns links whose owner contains the query, leaking/misattributing links.

findings.title: extend() revives already-expired links
findings.description: It unconditionally sets expires_at = now + ttl even for expired codes, contrary to documented finality.

findings.title: quotas() returns mutable reference to internal map
findings.description: Documented as a snapshot, but callers can mutate quota_ directly, bypassing accounting.

findings.title: import_all is not atomic and overrides duplicates
findings.description: Partial failures leave the store mutated, and validate_code is called per iteration after earlier writes; contradicts atomicity.

findings.title: prune() invalidates iterator and returns wrong count
findings.description: Erasing while incrementing is UB; it returns links_.size() instead of the removed count.

findings.title: last_code() returns dangling string_view
findings.description: Returns a view into the destroyed local `newest` string (and not the most recently created link).

findings.title: check_targets reads one past the vector end
findings.description: Loop bound `i <= links.size()` accesses links[size], undefined behavior.

findings.title: Janitor mutates store.all() while invalidating iterator
findings.description: Erasing from all() during iteration is UB.

findings.title: warm_cache threads are never joined
findings.description: joinable threads in the vector are destroyed at return, calling std::terminate.

findings.title: stop_janitor does not join the janitor thread
findings.description: The detached thread keeps running and the allocated thread* leaks; stopping is not synchronized.

findings.title: get() leaks expired Entry* after erase
findings.description: Erasing without deleting the Entry leaks memory on TTL expiry.

findings.title: Store links_ and quota_ mutated concurrently without synchronization
findings.description: Store exposes mutable containers (links_, quota_) with no mutex and non-const accessors such as all() and quotas(). The service runs request handlers on worker threads while the janitor thread iterates and erases entries via store.all(). Concurrent map reads/writes are data races with undefined behavior and can corrupt the link table or crash.

findings.title: Cache entries_ and hits_ accessed from multiple threads without a lock
findings.description: Cache::get/set/peek/erase/sweep/utilization and the hits_ counter touch shared state with no synchronization. warm_cache spawns threads calling cache.set concurrently, the janitor calls sweep, and request threads call get, so entries_ (including heap-allocated Entry*) and hits_ race, risking corruption, use-after-free of erased entries, and torn counters.

findings.title: Authenticator sessions map used without synchronization; verify returns dangling pointer
findings.description: issue, verify, revoke, and session_count mutate/read sessions_ from request threads with no lock. verify returns a pointer into the map, so a concurrent revoke or rehash can invalidate it, leaving callers (including handle()) with dangling references and causing use-after-free. Concurrent std::rand/std::map mutation in issue further contributes.

findings.title: Metrics counters are non-atomic and read without synchronization
findings.description: resolved_, created_, and errors_ are plain longs incremented from request threads and read in stats(). Concurrent non-atomic increments are data races (UB) and readers can observe torn/inconsistent counter values; errors_ is also never initialized.

findings.title: stop_janitor never joins the background thread
findings.description: stop_janitor() only sets g_running=false and leaves g_janitor running. On shutdown the janitor may keep accessing store/cache after they are destroyed, and the allocated thread is leaked. Repeated start/stop also reassigns g_janitor without joining the previous thread.

findings.title: warm_cache spawns per-link threads without joining them
findings.description: Each link spawns a thread that captures link by reference, but the threads are never joined. They can outlive the loop/function (dangling reference to the loop variable/link in the vector) and the cache is mutated concurrently without synchronization. Threads also leak, exhausting resources.

findings.title: Janitor erases store entries while iterating the returned map
findings.description: The janitor loop calls store.all().erase(it) on the same iterator it is incrementing in the for-loop. Erasing invalidates it before the loop's ++it, which is undefined behavior; combined with lock-free concurrent access to the store, this escalates to races and crashes.

findings.title: Session tokens are generated from std::rand
findings.description: issue() produces token text from two std::rand values. std::rand is not a cryptographic RNG and the default seed can be deterministic, making tokens predictable.

findings.title: verify() ignores session expiry
findings.description: The lookup returns a matching session even after expires_at has passed, so expired tokens remain valid indefinitely.

findings.title: require_admin() rejects every session
findings.description: The condition role != "admin" OR role != "owner" is always true, so even valid admin requests are rejected.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback secret is used when the environment is unset
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is missing or empty, the service uses the well-known value "dev-secret-do-not-use" instead of requiring configuration.

findings.title: Password storage uses a weak unsalted digest
findings.description: hash_password applies a 32-bit djb2-style hash directly to passwords, making it easy to brute force or collide.

findings.title: bearer_token copies an unbounded header into a fixed buffer
findings.description: strcpy into a 64-byte stack buffer can overflow, and the result of strchr is dereferenced without a null check.

findings.title: secret_equals leaks timing information
findings.description: Despite its documentation, it returns early on length or byte mismatches instead of performing a constant-time comparison.

findings.title: Cache destructor leaks Entry allocations
findings.description: Calling clear() destroys the map but never deletes the raw Entry* objects allocated by set().

findings.title: Eviction is not actually LRU
findings.description: set() evicts entries_.begin(), which is ordered by key rather than by least recent use.

findings.title: sweep() invalidates its iterator while erasing
findings.description: Erase is followed by iterator increment in the same loop, causing undefined behavior during expired-entry sweep.

findings.title: utilization() reports zero for non-full caches
findings.description: Integer division evaluates entries_.size() / limit_ before multiplication, so percentages below 100 truncate to zero.

findings.title: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS is mishandled and treated as seconds
findings.description: The milliseconds value is passed directly into Seconds, and bad values are only conditionally rejected.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is treated as seconds
findings.description: The milliseconds configuration value is used directly as Seconds, making cache TTLs 1000 times longer than configured.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but discarded
findings.description: parsed is explicitly cast to void, so the environment setting never affects the configuration.

findings.title: validate() returns success even when validation fails
findings.description: Problems are reported, but the function unconditionally returns true, allowing invalid deployments to continue.

findings.title: export_csv permits path traversal through the report name
findings.description: The user-controlled name is concatenated into the path despite comments saying it is confined to dir, allowing writes outside the export directory.

findings.title: archive_all permits path traversal through owner names
findings.description: Owner strings become file paths without sanitization, enabling writes outside the intended directory or file overwrite.

findings.title: write_snapshot uses a predictable fixed temporary path
findings.description: The global /tmp path is predictable, enabling symlink races and collisions, and rename() failure is ignored.

findings.title: Exported reports are created with default world-readable permissions
findings.description: The code intends service-user-only files but opens ofstream with default permissions.

findings.title: format_row returns a pointer to a destroyed stack buffer
findings.description: The returned const char* points to a local char array, resulting in undefined behavior for every caller.

findings.title: Metrics::errors_ is uninitialized
findings.description: errors_ has no default initializer unlike the other counters, so reading it before mutation is undefined behavior.

findings.title: all() exposes the private link map by mutable reference
findings.description: The store's internal map escapes ownership, allowing external mutation that bypasses validation and thread safety.

findings.title: create_link assumes required query parameters exist
findings.description: req.query.at() throws std::out_of_range for missing target or owner, and handle() does not catch that exception.

findings.title: delete_link lacks ownership authorization
findings.description: Any caller who knows a code can delete it because the authenticated owner is never compared with the link owner.

findings.title: admin_quotas trusts a spoofable x-admin header
findings.description: Administrator access is based solely on a client-supplied header instead of verifying the authenticated session role.

findings.title: stats() divides by store size without checking zero
findings.description: g_store->total_hits() / g_store->size() causes division by zero when there are no links.

findings.title: Authentication errors leak the submitted token
findings.description: The 401 response includes the rejected token value, exposing credential material.

findings.title: CORS allows credentials with a wildcard origin
findings.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with Allow-Credentials: true is unsafe and incompatibly configured for authenticated requests.

findings.title: Open redirect in /out endpoint
findings.description: The next parameter is used directly as the Location header without validation, enabling redirection to arbitrary destinations.

findings.title: resolve() has inverted expiry logic
findings.description: Links are deleted before expiry and accepted after expiry, so live links fail while expired links redirect.

findings.title: Short link codes use std::rand
findings.description: Code generation uses std::rand, making codes predictable and easier to guess or collide.

findings.title: rename() does not validate the destination code
findings.description: It validates from twice but never validates to, allowing invalid destination code replacement.

findings.title: page() computes an out-of-bounds slice end
findings.description: end is set to all.size()+1, so vector construction can read one element past the available range.

findings.title: success_rate() reports zero for most stores
findings.description: Integer division computes used / size before multiplying by 100, so any store below 100 percent usage reports zero percent.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending and can synthesize links
findings.description: The comparator uses < rather than descending order, and resize(n) can append default-constructed links.

findings.title: by_owner() matches substrings instead of exact owners
findings.description: It uses owner find(), so querying one owner also returns links owned by names containing that substring.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links
findings.description: The comment says expiry is final, but the implementation unconditionally sets expires_at to now plus ttl.

findings.title: quotas() returns a mutable internal reference
findings.description: Callers can mutate the quota map despite the documented snapshot semantics.

findings.title: import_all is not atomic and can overwrite duplicates
findings.description: Links are inserted one at a time, so partial imports and duplicate-code overwrites can happen.

findings.title: prune() invalidates its iterator while erasing
findings.description: Erase is followed by iterator increment, causing undefined behavior, and it returns store size instead of removed count.

findings.title: last_code() returns a dangling string_view
findings.description: newest is a local std::string destroyed on return, so the returned view points to freed memory.

findings.title: Janitor loop invalidates its iterator while erasing
findings.description: store.all().erase(it) is followed by iterator increment, causing undefined behavior on each sweep.

findings.title: Janitor mutates the store without synchronization
findings.description: The background thread accesses store.all() concurrently with request handlers, with no locking or atomics.

findings.title: warm_cache can terminate the process
findings.description: Worker threads are never joined or detached, causing their destructors to call std::terminate when the function returns.

findings.title: check_targets reads one element past the vector end
findings.description: The loop condition uses <= links.size(), causing an out-of-bounds access on the final iteration.

findings.title: stop_janitor does not join the worker thread
findings.description: Setting the flag leaves the janitor thread detached or leaked and creates shutdown race conditions.
